components.input_conditions: Square iid Gaussian factor; fixed-instance exact matrix-vector transcript; T<d.
components.parameter_and_cost_changes: Residual dimension d-T, factor variance 1/d, Gram scaling (d-T)/d relative to Wishart(d-T).
components.preserved_model_properties: The residual Gram matrix S is PSD and d/(d-T) times S has conditional Wishart(d-T) law.
remaining_obligations: Other ensembles and oracle permissions require separate lifting, outside this scope.
components.transcript_control: Appendix C.2 equation (8), base case and induction expose response blocks while preserving the conditional Gaussian residual.
components.transformation: Sequential left rotations align orthonormalized queries; right rotations align exposed Gaussian rows; retain the lower-right Gaussian block and its Gram matrix.

construction.definition: Sample X in R^{d by d} with independent N(0,1/d) entries once; set W=XX^T.
construction.hidden_objects: Sampled X and W; an unobserved residual Gaussian factor remains in the proof representation.
model_membership_refs: src.P088 revision 1, Definition 9, PDF p.9: Gaussian Gram construction; PSD follows from x^T W x=||X^T x||^2>=0.
construction.parameters: Positive integer d. For hardness, beta in (0,1), sufficiently large d(beta), and integer 0<=T<=floor((1-beta)d).
construction.public_information: Ambient dimension and Wishart sampling law; oracle access does not disclose X.

escape_conditions.epistemic_note: Model exclusions, not proved faster algorithms.
escape_conditions.statement: Revealing X or full W, charging multiple vectors as one query, or sampling fresh matrices falls outside this hardness claim.

hardness_claims.algorithm_coverage: Arbitrary adaptive randomized algorithms with seed independent of W; no Krylov or output-support restriction.
hardness_claims.missing_lifting: No transfer to other ensembles, entry/factor access, fresh-sample oracles, arithmetic runtime or other metrics.
hardness_claims.regime_note: For beta in (0,1), d>=ceil(N(sqrt(beta)/2)/beta), T<=floor((1-beta)d), additive error 1/(4d^2) has failure probability at least c_wish sqrt(beta), with universal local witness c_wish=exp(-3)/16.

oracle_realizations.choices_and_history: Queries may depend on previous queries, responses and algorithm randomness independent of W.
oracle_realizations.cost: One query per vector; no arithmetic-time bound or unit-cost batch access.
oracle_realizations.information_bottleneck: Lemma 13: after T orthonormalized queries, a query-dependent rotation gives blocks AA^T, AB^T, BA^T, BB^T+S, where A is T by T, B is (d-T) by T, and conditional on the transcript d/(d-T) times S has Wishart(d-T) law. Appendix C.2 constructs the residual Gaussian factor with entry variance 1/d.
oracle_realizations.information_to_error: The in-batch Theorem's local repair sets m=d-T, eps=1/(4d^2), a=sqrt(beta)/2 and d>=ceil(N(a)/beta). The PSD comparison, including singular A, gives lambda_min(W)<=lambda_min(S). Residual scaling gives q=P(lambda_min(S)<=eps)>=p0 sqrt(beta)/2; the full-matrix tail gives r=P(lambda_min(W)>=3eps)>=p0. Splitting any scalar output at 2eps yields p_error>=qr/(1+q)>=p0^2 sqrt(beta)/4. Here p0=exp(-3/2)/2 and N is defined in the Theorem local proof. This is a NEW proposed argument, not already accepted hardness.
oracle_realizations.query_and_feedback: Choose v in R^d and receive the complete exact vector Wv.
oracle_realizations.sampling_and_reuse: One sampled W reused throughout; no fresh matrices per query.
